Solve for $x$ in the figure above given that $KN=LN$ and $KP=LP.$
question.worked_solution:
By the converse of the perpendicular bisector theorem, a point equidistant from the endpoints of a segment lies on the perpendicular bisector of the segment. 

Here, the points $P$ and $N$ are both equidistant from the endpoints of $\overset{―}{KL}.$ Therefore, $P$ and $N$ both  lie on the perpendicular bisector of $\overset{―}{KL}.$ 

Since only one line can be drawn through two given points, the line $\overset{⟷}{PN}$ is the perpendicular bisector of $\overset{―}{KL}.$ 

In particular, we have that $KM=LM.$ We can use this equation to solve for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}KM & =LM \\ 2x+2 & =4x-6 \\ -2x & =-8 \\ x & =4\end{aligned}
$$
